text: The chair of the local {party} has a meeting coming up {meeting-when} and wants to know if you'll be there.
author: Codex writer B

text: The local committee meets {meeting-when}. As a member of the {party}, you're on the chair's invitation list.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can you join us {meeting-when}? It's the local committee meeting. I'd like to see you there.
author: Codex writer B

text: The committee meets {meeting-when}. Would you come sit with us?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm getting the committee together {meeting-when}. Can I put you down as coming?
author: Codex writer B

text: Will I see you {meeting-when}? That's when our local committee meets.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like you to meet the people who do the party work here. Could you come to the committee meeting {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: We're due to meet {meeting-when}, and I'd like to know who to expect. Will you be there?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come {meeting-when}. I'd like to hear what people bring up.
author: Codex writer B

text: Save me a seat. I want to see how the committee works.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put my name down for this meeting. I'll be there.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes, I'd like to meet the others who come. I'll see you {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me in. I'd be glad to start by listening.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll sit this one out. Thanks for thinking of me.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave me off the list for this meeting. I won't be there.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can't make it {meeting-when}. I'd still like to hear from you next time.
author: Codex writer B

text: Go ahead without me. I'm going to pass on this meeting.
author: Codex writer B

text: Thanks for asking. I'm not ready to come along this time.
author: Codex writer B

text: It was good to see you at the last committee meeting. Can you join us again {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: We're getting back together {meeting-when}. Shall I count you in again?
author: Codex writer B

text: Will you be with us {meeting-when}? I'd be glad to see you back at the committee.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll be back {meeting-when}. There are a few people I'd like to get to know better.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me in again. I'd like to speak up this time.
author: Codex writer B

text: I was glad I went last time. I'll have to miss the meeting {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll skip this one. Please keep asking me, though.
author: Codex writer B

text: You passed on the last meeting. Could you come {meeting-when} instead?
author: Codex writer B

text: Should I leave you off the list again, or can you join us {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: We're meeting {meeting-when}. I thought I'd ask again in case you can come this time.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can make this one. I'll see you {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: This time, put me down as coming. I'd like to meet the committee.
author: Codex writer B

text: I appreciate you asking again. I'll pass on this meeting too.
author: Codex writer B

text: No, I still won't be coming. Go ahead without me {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Last time you heard me talk about {prior-meeting-topic}. Will you come back {meeting-when}? I'd like to hear your take.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come. Give me a chance to hear the others on {prior-meeting-topic} before you call on me.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll pass this time. If you want my take on {prior-meeting-topic}, you can ask me here.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can you come {meeting-when}? I did the talking on {prior-meeting-topic} last time. What did I leave out?
author: Codex writer B

text: Save me a seat. There's a question on {prior-meeting-topic} I'd rather put to the whole room.
author: Codex writer B

text: I couldn't tell you what you missed. And I'll have to miss the meeting {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Will you come back {meeting-when}? You and {returning-member} have both been coming. Who else would you like to meet?
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down. If there's somebody new, I'd like to be the one to go over and say hello.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll skip this one. I don't have anybody in mind for an introduction.
author: Codex writer B

text: If {returning-member} comes again {meeting-when}, would you like a little time to talk before we get started?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd like to ask how people decide what to bring to the committee.
author: Codex writer B

text: Go ahead without me. I can arrange a conversation another day.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll save you a seat if you're coming {meeting-when}. If {returning-member} is there again, we can all sit together. Shall I count you in?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come. It'd be good to have somebody to sit down with.
author: Codex writer B

text: Thanks for making room for me. Leave me off the list this time.
author: Codex writer B

text: I've seen you and {returning-member} there twice running. Do you want to keep coming when we meet {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I want to stick around long enough to see what comes of the things people bring up.
author: Codex writer B

text: I wanted to see how it worked. I've done that. Count me out for this meeting.
author: Codex writer B

text: I said a worker ought to be able to turn down the union fee and keep the job. Will you come {meeting-when}? I'd like to hear what you think it would mean on payday.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down. I want to hear who pays for bargaining if somebody opts out.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave me off this time. I'd rather talk it over with somebody who works under one of those contracts first.
author: Codex writer B

text: Coming {meeting-when}? You heard my case for letting people opt out of the fee. If you had the floor instead of me, where would you start?
author: Codex writer B

text: With the paycheck. What does a worker actually get to decide? I'll come.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll pass. I don't want the floor, and I don't want anybody waiting on me to take it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Last time I asked why keeping a job should depend on paying the union. Can you come {meeting-when}, even if you'd answer that differently?
author: Codex writer B

text: Save me a chair. I like a meeting where you can answer a question like that out loud.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me out for this one. You can ask the room without me.
author: Codex writer B

text: I made the case for collecting a share of bargaining costs from everyone the contract covers. Will you come {meeting-when}? Was there a question you wanted to get in?
author: Codex writer B

text: There was. Who works out what's a fair share? I'll come and ask.
author: Codex writer B

text: I think I heard you right the first time. I'll sit this meeting out.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose the contract gets you a raise and you didn't pay toward bargaining. That's the case I put to the room last time. Coming back {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd like to hear how the person getting that paycheck would put it.
author: Codex writer B

text: You can leave me off. I'd like to think that one through on my own.
author: Codex writer B

text: You heard where I stand on bargaining fees. Can you come {meeting-when}? I'd rather have you ask me about the fee than go home wondering what it pays for.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down. I'd like to know how much of the work happens after the contract's signed.
author: Codex writer B

text: Go ahead without me. If I've got a question for you, I'll ask you myself.
author: Codex writer B

text: Last time you heard me say a worker should be able to refuse the fee. That's my view. The committee can't change anybody's paycheck. Will you come {meeting-when} and tell me who you think ought to hear it?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. When I come {meeting-when}, I'd like to ask what it would take for a worker to get that choice.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll pass {meeting-when}. I heard your argument. I want to find out what the law says first.
author: Codex writer B

text: Say everybody in the room agreed with me about letting workers turn down the fee. What would that change when somebody reports for work the next morning? I'd like to hear your answer if you can come {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down for the {party} meeting. My first question would be who has the power to change what the worker owes.
author: Codex writer B

text: I won't be there {meeting-when}. That's a fair question, but I'd just be guessing at the answer.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can you make the meeting {meeting-when}? You heard why I'd let somebody keep the job without paying the fee. Coming to hear me out didn't put you on my side, and coming back wouldn't either.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come {meeting-when}. I can ask what an opt-out would mean without putting my name to it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave me off the list {meeting-when}. I'd like to talk with someone who works under a contract before I take that up again.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like some company {meeting-when}. You know where I stand on the fee. If I asked a lawmaker to let a worker opt out of it, what's the first question you'd want me to take along?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll be there. My question for the {party} is who would still have to cover the cost of bargaining.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm staying home {meeting-when}. I haven't got a question I'd want you to carry in my name.
author: Codex writer B

text: The case I made was about paying for bargaining when the contract covers everybody. The committee can ask for that rule. It can't take the fee out of anybody's pay. Could you come {meeting-when} and talk about the difference?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd like to ask the {party} which part would take a change in the law.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me out {meeting-when}. I heard what you want. I'd like to read up on who could actually do it.
author: Codex writer B

text: When I spoke, I argued for sharing bargaining costs. Would you come {meeting-when}? I'm interested in what you'd ask somebody who could change the law, even if you wouldn't ask them to change it.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come {meeting-when}. I'd ask whether a worker who doesn't join would pay for anything beyond representation.
author: Codex writer B

text: I won't come {meeting-when}. I'd rather work out my own question before giving it to somebody else to ask.
author: Codex writer B

text: You've heard me argue that a contract costs money to negotiate. If everybody in the room agreed with me about sharing the bill, that still wouldn't change a contract. Will I see you {meeting-when}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd like to hear what the {party} could reasonably ask a legislator to do about that cost.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll sit this one out {meeting-when}. I understand what you're asking for. I haven't made up my mind about the fee.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's a difference between saying who ought to help pay for bargaining and telling a worker what they owe. I spoke about what I think is fair. Would you join us {meeting-when} and bring the question that leaves you with?
author: Codex writer B

text: I can come {meeting-when}. I'd ask who decides which expenses count as bargaining.
author: Codex writer B

text: Don't count on me {meeting-when}. I'd rather hear how that fee gets worked out at a workplace before I talk about it at a committee meeting.
author: Codex writer B

text: I wonder what you'd tell somebody who missed my talk about {prior-meeting-topic}. Come sit with me {meeting-when} if you can. I'd like to hear what stuck.
author: Codex writer B

text: Over a cup of coffee, maybe. I'll come {meeting-when}, and you can hear the short version.
author: Codex writer B

text: You'll have to count me out {meeting-when}. I heard you, but I wouldn't try to repeat it for somebody else.
author: Codex writer B

text: I could use an honest answer. When I talked about {prior-meeting-topic}, where did I lose you? Let me buy you a coffee {meeting-when} and you can tell me.
author: Codex writer B

text: Black coffee for me. I'll see you {meeting-when}. I did have a question about how that would work.
author: Codex writer B

text: Keep the coffee money. I'm passing {meeting-when}, and it was your conclusion I had trouble with.
author: Codex writer B

text: Do you know anybody else in the room yet? You heard me on {prior-meeting-topic}, but you'd get a different sort of conversation sitting beside somebody new {meeting-when}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like that. Come find me {meeting-when} and introduce me to somebody who sees it differently.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave me off the list {meeting-when}. Meeting a roomful of people still feels too much like work.
author: Codex writer B

text: I had my say about {prior-meeting-topic}. Your turn, if you want it. Could you come {meeting-when} with one question you'd actually like somebody to answer?
author: Codex writer B

text: I can bring one {meeting-when}. Can I ask it in my own words?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll sit this one out. I don't have a question about {prior-meeting-topic} I want to ask a whole room.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose somebody walked in halfway through what I said about {prior-meeting-topic}. Where should I have started? Come back {meeting-when} and help me figure that out.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with who it affects. I'll come {meeting-when} and tell you why I'd start there.
author: Codex writer B

text: I won't make it {meeting-when}. My advice would be to ask somebody who's hearing it for the first time.
author: Codex writer B

text: The meeting is {meeting-when}. If you come early, we can talk about {prior-meeting-topic} without either of us having to address the room. Would that suit you?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd rather have that talk with you before the {party} meeting gets going.
author: Codex writer B

text: No, go ahead without me {meeting-when}. If I ever take that up with you, I'd like other people there to hear the answer.
author: Codex writer B

text: Do you want to walk in with me {meeting-when}? You passed last time, and I know how it feels to open a door onto a roomful of people who know each other.
author: Codex writer B

text: Meet me outside and we'll go in together. I'd like that.
author: Codex writer B

text: I appreciate the offer. Keep your usual plans for getting there. I'm staying home this time.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would an introduction help? If you come {meeting-when}, I'll start with somebody who knows this district from one end to the other.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. I'd like to meet the person who can tell me which neighborhoods I still need to get out and see.
author: Codex writer B

text: Hold off on the introduction. I don't want somebody waiting around for a person who isn't coming.
author: Codex writer B

text: I left you off the list last time, like you asked. We're meeting {meeting-when}. Mind if I put your name down this time?
author: Codex writer B

text: Go ahead and write it down. I'll be there.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave a space for somebody else. I still mean to keep that evening free.
author: Codex writer B

text: Last time didn't work out. If you came {meeting-when}, is there anybody in the committee room you'd want to sit with?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd sit with you, if you don't mind. You can tell me who's speaking until I get the names straight.
author: Codex writer B

text: Don't save a chair for me. I won't be at this one either.
author: Codex writer B

text: What about coming {meeting-when} just to listen? You can decide afterward whether you want any part in the committee's work.
author: Codex writer B

text: That suits me. I'll come hear what people spend their meeting time on before I offer to help.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can listen another evening. I'd rather tell you now so you know who's coming.
author: Codex writer B

text: The committee meets {meeting-when}. Is that a date you can commit to, or should I count you out for the evening?
author: Codex writer B

text: Let's try again. This time you can count me in.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll ask about a later meeting. Count me out for this one.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could you come by {meeting-when}? I'd like to spread out a street map and hear where you think we'd be knocking on doors somebody already covered.
author: Codex writer B

text: Bring the map. I'll come early enough to look it over with you.
author: Codex writer B

text: Take the map along without me. I won't be there to go over it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Are you free {meeting-when}? Come sit by me if you'd like to hear how somebody gets picked to represent a precinct.
author: Codex writer B

text: Save me that seat. I've always wondered who gets to put a name forward.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give that seat to somebody else. I'm going to miss the meeting again.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can you make it {meeting-when}? If somebody asks whether you'd ever stand for precinct office, you're allowed to say you just came to hear about it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Then I'll come. I can ask what the job takes without volunteering for it on the spot.
author: Codex writer B

text: Skip me this time. I don't feel like spending my evening explaining why I'm not running for anything.
author: Codex writer B

text: Come along {meeting-when}? If you've ever wondered what happens to a resolution after the party adopts it, we could talk about that on the way in.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll meet you outside. I'd like to hear who has to take it up before it can become law.
author: Codex writer B

text: Another evening, maybe. I've got a question about those resolutions, but I'll save it until we see each other again.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come. Can we mark the streets the regulars want to keep? I'd sooner take a block nobody has walked.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down for the meeting. Before we hand out addresses I want to check where the other crew stops.
author: Codex writer B

text: You should do the map without me. I couldn't tell you which doors the regulars have tried, and I won't be there to ask.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll pass this time. Please leave my name off the map if you're dividing up streets.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like that. When somebody offers to take a precinct, who actually makes it official? I'll come sit with you.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes, keep me a chair. I want to see what the secretary writes down when a neighbor gets the job.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can't come. Let me know afterward who to ask about a precinct opening.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm staying home. If someone else wants to see how the appointment works, give them the seat.
author: Codex writer B

text: Sure, I'll come. I might know somebody who'd run, even if I don't put my own name in.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll be there. I'd like to hear a precinct officer describe a week on the job before I decide anything.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm going to pass. I'm willing to look for somebody who might run. That's as far as I want to go.
author: Codex writer B

text: Thanks for making that clear. I'd still rather miss this one than spend the evening turning people down.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me in. I'm curious who would have to introduce a bill if the committee got behind the idea.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come hear it. A party vote I understand. The part I lose track of is who takes it to the legislature.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll skip the meeting. I'd still like to hear what became of that resolution when we next have coffee.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can't join you. If somebody takes the resolution to a legislator, that's the part I'd like to hear about afterward.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like that. Will you point out somebody who knows my end of town?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll be there. Just give me a name when I get there. I can go say hello myself.
author: Codex writer B

text: Save me a chair by you. I'd like to put faces to the names I keep hearing.
author: Codex writer B

text: Sure. Who's been coming the longest? That's who I'd like to sit with.
author: Codex writer B

text: Count me in. If there's a job people stay late to do, introduce me to whoever usually gets stuck doing it.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll pass this time. Could we have coffee with one of them instead? I'd get more out of that.
author: Codex writer B

text: Please go ahead without me. I'd hate to have you walking around looking for me when it's time to introduce people.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can't come. Is there somebody in my neighborhood I could walk over and introduce myself to?
author: Codex writer B

text: Another time. I'd like to meet them when I can stay and talk.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave me off for now. I haven't made up my mind about doing party work, and I'd like to tell you that before you introduce me around.
author: Codex writer B

text: Meet me at the door and take me in with you, will you? I hate standing around trying to guess who's in charge.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would it be all right if I listened for a while first? Once I hear people talk, their names tend to stick.
author: Codex writer B

text: If you see somebody from my precinct, wave me over. I'll get there before the meeting starts.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll come early enough to help set up. It's easier to get talking when you're both unfolding chairs.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who tells the best stories? Save me a place by them. I want to hear how everybody got mixed up in this business.
author: Codex writer B

text: Tell them I'm coming. They may know me by sight already, but I doubt they know my name.
author: Codex writer B
